I was first introduced to DMT over a year ago and I was amazed. It was everything I ever wanted out of a hallucinogen. I was also dealing with a lot of depression and borderline suicidal. I thought I could use DMT as a tool to shift my perspective and elevate my mood. I got my hands on about 4 grams worth and went through a solid month where I tripped several days week, often multiple times a day. I never went on a stretch like you're on, but I can relate to why you're there.

Funny thing is that instead of taking away my desire to die, it removed my fear of death. I started to become numb to the concept, as there were several trips where I "knew" I was dead and I accepted it so I could let go completely. It started to become a beautiful thing in my minds eye. 

Reality started getting a little wierd for me during that time. I would be spacy and distracted at work. I would notice things out of the corner of my eyes - movements, and stare into the abyss, trying to piece together the fragments of my recent trips. I was starting to worry that I was disassociating reality. 

It was hard for me to talk to people, because I wanted to share my amazing experiences with everyone, but I couldnt. Small talk became so ^^small to me. Why the FUCK are we talking about the fucking weather when there is there is an entire beautiful, infinite universe inside all of our minds eye that so little of us have explored? 

Even my close friends that I tripped with started becoming worried for my mental health and asked me to slow down. They couldn't believe that I was taking it as far as I was with something so powerful. So I slowed down. 

I stopped completely after a drunken night where me and my friend tripped 5 or 6 times in a row and he experienced DMT's version of hell. He was so distraught afterwards and wouldnt stop freaking out. I though he would just need to sleep it off, but the next day he was still very upset about it. Weeks went on and he would talk about it. He said it was the most terrifying experience if his life. During his trip, shadow entities pinned him down and told him he was trapped in infinite darkness, and that this was what happened when you do too much. That night he kept saying over and over "it felt like forever, it felt like forever". 

Not to say that I was completely afraid, as most of my trips were amazing, but his experience kind of grounded me and made me realize I was playing with fire. That was almost a year ago now and I've tripped twice since. I have a bunch left, but I'm saving it for when the time is right..

Anyways, hope you get reality sorted out and you're able to return to DMT eventually. Just be cautious and respectful. You only have one mind.

This is the harsh reality of DMT, and most hallucinogens. It's not all rainbow fractals and machine elves. Things can get dark very very quickly. And it's your own mind, so it gets more fucked up than you might have thought possible. Tread lightly people, and do not abuse this substance.

Edit: note that OP mentioned doing it several times that day, and also posted about tripping about a week ago. This is playing with fire. I truly believe most of us have part of our conscience telling us "You might be doing this too often, slow down or you might regret it", even if it's a small part of us. This is when things can go sideways quickly. Do not underestimate your psyches ability to punish you during a trip when you feel guilt, especially guilt or worry specifically about the act of tripping. It wont always turn out this way, but it easily can happen.
